messages:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to rewrite the console -> query dependency surface into a compact facade + auth preflight. Goal: smaller per-request payloads, push RBAC checks earlier, and make canary rollouts cheaper. Thoughts?

alex: sounds good. can you sketch the new request flow? curious how we handle panel-level perms and existing projection logic. :thinking:

maya: high level: 1) console constructs a compact intent proto (route id, projection set, tenant id, client hints) instead of full query graph 2) query-facade performs auth preflight + simple routing 3) facade expands to internal engine calls only for allowed fields 4) keep an escape hatch for legacy complex queries.

kevin: how big is the proto vs current payload? main concern is added serialization cost vs network.

maya: rough numbers from bench: full client graph ~1.8KB avg, proto intent ~220B. drops parse time by ~10-15ms at the facade edge. also enables cheaper cache keys.

zoe: important: RBAC enforcement earlier means we must canonicalize projections so auth policy can reason about them. otherwise we risk under/over-exposing data. we should formalize a minimal projection grammar.

alex: agree on grammar. also need to preserve ability for panels that depend on dynamic post-aggregation filters. can we support a small DSL in the intent?

maya: plan is to keep intent expressive for route-level projections and filters, but not the full AST. for heavy queries, console can call legacy /query endpoint (marked heavy) — that path goes to a dedicated pool with stricter SLOs and audit.

kevin: what about canary rollout? we should avoid big cutovers. proposal: 1) deploy facade behind feature flag 2) 5% traffic to facade with shadowing to legacy 3) enable auth-preflight in strict mode only for canary 4) monitor error budget and latency.

zoe: metrics to track: auth_mismatch_count, facade_expansion_failures, percent_of_heavy_queries, avg_end_to_end_latency_by_route, cache_hit_ratio_on_intent_key. Also add an audit log for escaped legacy queries.

alex: how do we version the intent contract? frontends must be able to fall back if facade doesn't understand a newer intent.

maya: explicit version header in the intent payload: `X-Intent-Version`. fallback semantics: if facade returns 412, console falls back to legacy path. We'll maintain two versions concurrently for 3 months per release.

kevin: ops ask: any additional infra cost? facade will be light CPU but needs to be HA at edge. might be more instances but lower compute per-request. also we can colocate with gateway service.

maya: agreed. we can co-locate with existing console api gateways to reuse TLS and rate limits. autoscale policy tuned for short CPU spikes.

zoe: security note: preflight must call our central policy engine (OPA) with normalized projection. watch out for amplification attacks where many small intents cause OPA storm. consider batching OPA checks for a tenant or route when possible.

alex: +1 batch checks, and add a small LRU for recent allow results keyed by (tenant, route, projection-hash). TTL like 30s should be safe.

maya: good call. caching auth results reduces steady-state latency but we’ll invalidate on role-change webhook.

kevin: migration checklist idea: 1) implement facade with feature flag 2) shadow expansions for all canary traffic 3) enable preflight for read-only routes first 4) enable for interactive dashboards 5) roll legacy-heavy as needed.

maya: I'll draft a small RFC doc with the grammar sketch and rollout checklist. embedding a tiny example intent payload:```
{
  "intent_v":"1",
  "route":"dashboard_tile.v2",
  "tenant":"t-42",
  "projection":["user.name","usage.agg30"],
  "hints":{"max_rows":100,"prefetch":true}
}
```

zoe: looks good. can we also include a mapping table of common legacy graph nodes -> projection terms so the facade expansion can be deterministic?

maya: yes, mapping table included in RFC. I'll add compatibility tests that compare legacy output vs facade-expanded output for a sample set of panels.

infra-bot: CI pipeline: integration-tests/console-facade failed on staging (auth-suite) — see https://ci.redwood.internal/12345 :warning:

kevin: thanks infra-bot. maya, the failing test is likely the role-change invalidation. add the webhook binding in the test harness.

maya: noted. I'll push a patch with the webhook and a small LRU tweak. planning to post the RFC this afternoon for async review. :thumbsup:
